Events.RelatedBody: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. The Blazor WebAssembly development-server debug page can reflect unencoded exception text, allowing cross-origin script injection through the unauthenticated `/_framework/debug` endpoint used by `dotnet watch`. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/discussions/69802 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 8.8 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-79 (Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Windows, Linux, macOS - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages The vulnerability affects Microsoft .NET projects that use an affected package version listed below. Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | --------------- [Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server) | >= 10.0.0, <= 10.0.12 | 10.0.13 [Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server) | >= 11.0.0-preview.1, <= 11.0.0-rc.1 | 11.0.0-rc.2 [Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.31 | 8.0.32 [Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server) | >= 9.0.0, <= 9.0.20 | 9.0.21 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? If using a package listed in [affected packages](#affected-packages), you're exposed to the vulnerability. ### How do I fix the issue? 1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET. If you have installed one or more .NET SDKs through Visual Studio, Visual Studio will prompt you to update Visual Studio, which will also update your .NET SDKs. 2. If your application references the vulnerable package, update the package reference to the patched version. You can list the versions you have installed by running the `dotnet --info` command. * If you're using .NET 8.0, you should download and install .NET 8.0.32 Runtime or .NET 8.0.426 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/8.0. * If you're using .NET 9.0, you should download and install .NET 9.0.21 Runtime or .NET 9.0.319 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/9.0. * If you're using .NET 10.0, you should download and install .NET 10.0.13 Runtime or .NET 10.0.402 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/10.0. * If you're using .NET 11.0, you should download and install .NET 11.0.0-rc.2 Runtime or .NET 11.0.100-rc.2 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/11.0. Once you have installed the updated runtime or SDK, restart your apps for the update to take effect. Additionally, if you've deployed [self-contained applications](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/deploying/#self-contained-deployments-scd) targeting any of the impacted versions, these applications are also vulnerable and must be recompiled and redeployed. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. The main repos are located at https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. Microsoft disclaims all warranties, either express or implied, including the warranties of merchantability and fitness for a particular purpose. In no event shall Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers be liable for any damages whatsoever including direct, indirect, incidental, consequential, loss of business profits or special damages, even if Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers have been advised of the possibility of such damages. Some states do not allow the exclusion or limitation of liability for consequential or incidental damages so the foregoing limitation may not apply. ### External Links [CVE-2026-96230](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-96230) ### Acknowledgements - Kevin Gosse ### Revisions V1.0 (10/13/2026): Advisory published.

### Describe the bug

`dotnet run --file` reuses the cached build of a file-based app even when a required package dependency DLL is missing from the cached output directory. It then crashes with `FileNotFoundException`, instead of rebuilding/copying the missing dependency.

This was first observed with a small file-based utility referencing `NuGet.Configuration` and `NuGet.Packaging`. The cause of the original DLL disappearance is unknown. The following minimal repro deliberately removes one output DLL to demonstrate the cache-validation problem deterministically; it does not delete anything from the global NuGet package cache.

### Steps to reproduce

On Windows with PowerShell, create `repro.cs` in an otherwise empty directory:

```csharp
#:package NuGet.Configuration@7.3.1

Console.WriteLine(typeof(NuGet.Configuration.Settings).Assembly.Location);
```

Run:

```powershell
# Build and run successfully; capture the copied dependency's location.
$dll = dotnet run --file .\repro.cs | Select-Object -Last 1
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0 -or !(Test-Path -LiteralPath $dll)) {
    throw "Initial run failed or dependency path was not found."
}

# Remove only this file-based app's copied dependency DLL.
# The path printed above is under:
# %TEMP%\dotnet\runfile\repro-<hash>\bin\debug\NuGet.Configuration.dll
Remove-Item -LiteralPath $dll

# No source/input changes. This reuses the incomplete cache and crashes.
dotnet run --file .\repro.cs

# Force the build: succeeds and restores the missing DLL.
dotnet run --no-cache --file .\repro.cs
Test-Path -LiteralPath $dll # True
```

The `Assembly.Location` access may produce an IL3000 warning on the initial build; the normal `dotnet run` execution nevertheless prints the DLL's actual path. This exact minimal program was tested successfully before deleting the DLL, failed after deleting it, and succeeded again with `--no-cache`.

### Expected behavior

Without `--no-build`, `dotnet run --file` detects that a required runtime output is missing, invokes the build to restore it, and runs successfully. An incomplete cached build should not be considered up to date.

### Actual behavior

The second normal run skips the build and fails:

```text
Unhandled exception. System.IO.FileNotFoundException: Could not load file or assembly 'NuGet.Configuration, Version=7.3.1.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=31bf3856ad364e35'. The system cannot find the file specified.
File name: 'NuGet.Configuration, Version=7.3.1.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=31bf3856ad364e35'
Requested by: sdk-missing-dependency-repro, Version=1.0.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=null
 --> System.Private.CoreLib, Version=11.0.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=7cec85d7bea7798e
   at Program.<Main>$(String[] args)
```

The host also reports that it cannot open `%TEMP%\dotnet\runfile\<app>-<hash>\bin\debug\NuGet.Configuration.dll` with error `0x80070002`.

Exit code observed: `-532462766`.

### Is this a regression?

Unknown; verified with SDK `11.0.100-rc.2.26504.105`. Other SDK versions have not been tested.

### Are there any workarounds?

Use `dotnet run --no-cache --file .\repro.cs`. This restores the missing DLL and runs successfully, but forces the build on every invocation.

 MSBuild version: 18.12.0-1.26504.105+820230c38

Possibly related symptoms: dotnet/sdk#53732. That issue was closed after a fix involving `#:project` dependency changes. This repro uses only a direct `#:package` reference, no referenced projects, no concurrent execution, and an explicitly removed runtime output on a newer SDK.

Use `dotnet run --no-cache --file .\repro.cs`. This restores the missing DLL and runs successfully, but forces the build on every invocation.

### Environment

```text

 Version:         11.0.100-rc.2.26504.105
 Commit:          820230c386
 MSBuild version: 18.12.0-1.26504.105+820230c38

Runtime Environment:

 Commit:          820230c386

Environment variables:

global.json:

```

Reproduced from the command line without an IDE.

### Related issue

Possibly related symptoms: dotnet/sdk#53732. That issue was closed after a fix involving `#:project` dependency changes. This repro uses only a direct `#:package` reference, no referenced projects, no concurrent execution, and an explicitly removed runtime output on a newer SDK.

### Describe the bug

`dotnet run --file` reuses the cached build of a file-based app even when a required package dependency DLL is missing from the cached output directory. It then crashes with `FileNotFoundException`, instead of rebuilding/copying the missing dependency.

This was first observed with a small file-based utility referencing `NuGet.Configuration` and `NuGet.Packaging`. The cause of the original DLL disappearance is unknown. The following minimal repro deliberately removes one output DLL to demonstrate the cache-validation problem deterministically; it does not delete anything from the global NuGet package cache.

### Steps to reproduce

On Windows with PowerShell, create `repro.cs` in an otherwise empty directory:

```csharp
#:package NuGet.Configuration@7.3.1

Console.WriteLine(typeof(NuGet.Configuration.Settings).Assembly.Location);
```

Run:

```powershell
# Build and run successfully; capture the copied dependency's location.
$dll = dotnet run --file .\repro.cs | Select-Object -Last 1
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0 -or !(Test-Path -LiteralPath $dll)) {
    throw "Initial run failed or dependency path was not found."
}

# Remove only this file-based app's copied dependency DLL.
# The path printed above is under:
# %TEMP%\dotnet\runfile\repro-<hash>\bin\debug\NuGet.Configuration.dll
Remove-Item -LiteralPath $dll

# No source/input changes. This reuses the incomplete cache and crashes.
dotnet run --file .\repro.cs

# Force the build: succeeds and restores the missing DLL.
dotnet run --no-cache --file .\repro.cs
Test-Path -LiteralPath $dll # True
```

The `Assembly.Location` access may produce an IL3000 warning on the initial build; the normal `dotnet run` execution nevertheless prints the DLL's actual path. This exact minimal program was tested successfully before deleting the DLL, failed after deleting it, and succeeded again with `--no-cache`.

### Expected behavior

Without `--no-build`, `dotnet run --file` detects that a required runtime output is missing, invokes the build to restore it, and runs successfully. An incomplete cached build should not be considered up to date.

### Actual behavior

The second normal run skips the build and fails:

```text
Unhandled exception. System.IO.FileNotFoundException: Could not load file or assembly 'NuGet.Configuration, Version=7.3.1.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=31bf3856ad364e35'. The system cannot find the file specified.
File name: 'NuGet.Configuration, Version=7.3.1.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=31bf3856ad364e35'
Requested by: sdk-missing-dependency-repro, Version=1.0.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=null
 --> System.Private.CoreLib, Version=11.0.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=7cec85d7bea7798e
   at Program.<Main>$(String[] args)
```

The host also reports that it cannot open `%TEMP%\dotnet\runfile\<app>-<hash>\bin\debug\NuGet.Configuration.dll` with error `0x80070002`.

Exit code observed: `-532462766`.

### Is this a regression?

Unknown; verified with SDK `11.0.100-rc.2.26504.105`. Other SDK versions have not been tested.

Issues.Title: [release/3.1] Reset current_no_gc_region_info after leaving no gc region implicitly
Issues.Body:
Backport https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/73602.

## Customer Impact
Customers reported occasional `System.InvalidOperationException` with message `The NoGCRegion mode was already in progress` when calling `GC.TryStartNoGCRegion`. This is preventing them from using this optimization and impacting their cold start latencies.

## Testing
Customers have tried the fix on .NET 6 overnight and reported the exception never appears again. Meanwhile, there is an unpatched machine and observed 72 exceptions of the same type in the same time interval, proving this does fix the bug.

## Risk
Low. This only impact customer using `TryStartNoGCRegion`, and this is the right thing to do.

Issues.Title: Migrate FabricBot Tasks to Config-as-Code
Issues.Body:
**TL;DR;** Requesting to add [FabricBot](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/fabricbot_overview) configuration associated with your repository to `.github/fabricbot.json`.

**Context**

FabricBot is now a [config-as-code-only](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/bot-config-as-code) platform. As a result, while you can still use the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/coreclr) to modify your FabricBot configuration, you can no longer save the changes. The only way to save changes to your configuration at the moment is to _export configuration_ from the portal and upload the exported configuration to `.github/fabricbot.json` in your repository. In this pull request, we are adding your FabricBot configuration to your repository at `.github/fabricbot.json` so that you can make changes to it going forward.

While the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/coreclr) is the *only way* to modify your FabricBot configuration at the moment, we have a feature on our backlog to publish the JSON schema defining the structure of the FabricBot configuration file. With the JSON schema, you can (1) use a plaintext editor of your choice to modify the FabricBot configuration file and use the schema to validate the file after editing or (2) [configure](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/languages/json#_json-schemas-and-settings) VS Code to use the schema when editing FabricBot configuration file to take advantage of convenience features such as automatic code completion and field description on mouseover.

[*Pull Request Create*](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/prcreate), a [MerlinBot](https://https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot) Extension, was used to automatically create this pull request. If you have any questions or concerns with this pull request, please contact [MerlinBot Expert DRI](mailto:merlinbotdri@microsoft.com).

The only way to save changes to your configuration at the moment is to _export configuration_ from the portal and upload the exported configuration to `.github/fabricbot.json` in your repository. In this pull request, we are adding your FabricBot configuration to your repository at `.github/fabricbot.json` so that you can make changes to it going forward.

While the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/cli) is the *only way* to modify your FabricBot configuration at the moment, we have a feature on our backlog to publish the JSON schema defining the structure of the FabricBot configuration file. With the JSON schema, you can (1) use a plaintext editor of your choice to modify the FabricBot configuration file and use the schema to validate the file after editing or (2) [configure](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/languages/json#_json-schemas-and-settings) VS Code to use the schema when editing FabricBot configuration file to take advantage of convenience features such as automatic code completion and field description on mouseover.

Issues.Title: Questions about tagging within this repository / future versions
Issues.Body:
I was looking through this repository to determine if .NET Standard 2.1 libraries support default interface methods - it looks like they do, given the presence of `System.Runtime.CompilerServices.RuntimeFeature.DefaultImplementationsOfInterfaces`, as well as my own experimenting in VS 2019. It seems I was mistaken when thinking that this was not the case, so I'm glad this repository is easily accessible to determine this.

But while doing this, I found it difficult to determine what commits were included in this particular .NET Standard version. I see that there's a tag `v2.1.0-prerelease.19126.1`, as well as branches `release/2.0.0`, `release/3.0`, and `release/3.0-preview9`. One of the machines I tested VS 2019 on had a `netstandard.dll` assembly, itself targeting .NETStandard v2.1.0, with AssemblyInformationalVersion `1.1.0+a5b5f2e1e369972c8ff1e2183979fab6099f52ef`; this commit is part of the `release/3.0` branch. However, another machine had a same-named assembly, targeting .NETCoreApp v3.0 and AssemblyInformationalVersion `3.0.0+4ac4c0367003fe3973a3648eb0715ddb0e3bbcea`, and I don't see that commit hash in this repository.

Additionally, [this blog post](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/dotnet/the-future-of-net-standard/) states that 2.1 will be the last version, but there is another prerelease tag `v2.2.0-prerelease.19564.1` and [on GitHub](https://github.com/dotnet/standard/releases/tag/v2.2.0-prerelease.19564.1) it's labelled .NET 5.0 Preview 2.

So I have a few questions for understanding this repository:

1. Since .NET Standard 2.1 is released, are there plans to continue development in this repository for e.g. the shared BCL going forward with .NET 5+?
2. Are there multiple kinds of `netstandard.dll` for a single .NET Standard version? E.g. are there separate versions for .NET Framework to reference and for .NET Core / .NET 5+ to reference?
3. Do the tags / branch names in this repository correspond to a .NET Standard version or something else?
4. It looks like there are patch releases; are there patch versions of a single .NET Standard version?
5. Are there other repositories which are being used to create `netstandard.dll`?
6. Is there a way to determine, from the repository, which commit is the one used for a given release?

Thank you for your consideration.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Questions about tagging within this repository / future versions" (#1777)

Issues.Title: Issue with resolving between .NET Standard 2.0 and .NET Standard 2.1
Issues.Body:
# Summary

.NET Standard version is not resolved correctly when a transitive dependency targets multiple .NET Standard versions.

# Environment

- Windows 10 (19042.746)
- .NET 5 SDK 5.0.201

# Minimal reproducible example
[bug.zip](https://github.com/dotnet/standard/files/6209239/bug.zip)

This is a three-project solution:
- `TestProject1` targeting `netcoreapp3.1`
- `ClassProject1` targeting `netstandard2.0`
- `ClassProject2` targeting *both* `netstandard2.0` and `netstandard2.1`

The project dependency chain is: `TestProject1 -> ClassProject1 -> ClassProject2`

A method (`ClassProject2Test1`) on `ClassProject2` is hidden behind a `#if NETSTANDARD2_0` preprocessor directive.

# The issue

The unit test failed with a `MissingMethodException`

```
[xUnit.net 00:00:00.38]     TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1 [FAIL]
  Failed TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1 [2 ms]
  Error Message:
   System.MissingMethodException : Method not found: 'Void ClassLibrary2.Class2.Class2Test1()'.
  Stack Trace:
     at ClassLibrary1.Class1.Class1Test1()
   at TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1() in C:\Users\rex\source\netstandard-bug-repro\TestProject1\UnitTest1.cs:line 12
```

# Expected result

The compiler should have resolved the chain as:

`TestProject1 (.NET Core 3.1) -> ClassProject1 (.NET Standard 2.0) -> *ClassProject2 (.NET Standard 2.0)*` 

# Actual result

The compiler resolved the chain as:

`TestProject1 (.NET Core 3.1) -> ClassProject1 (.NET Standard 2.0) -> *ClassProject2 (.NET Standard 2.1)*` 

Which causes the exception because the offending method, `ClassProject2Test1`, was hidden by the `#if NETSTANDARD2_0` preprocessor directive.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Issue with resolving between .NET Standard 2.0 and .NET Standard 2.1" (#1787)

Issues.Title: Security Vulnerability due to System.Text.RegularExpressions
Issues.Body:
### Problem
There is a security vulnerability with the version of System.Text.RegularExpressions that is used by dotnet standard. The vulnerable version of System.Text.RegularExpressions is 4.3.0. Please see links below for the vulnerability documentation or discussion:

https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/en-US/vulnerability/CVE-2019-0820
https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/111
https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2019-0820
https://snyk.io/vuln/SNYK-DOTNET-SYSTEMTEXTREGULAREXPRESSIONS-174708
https://www.whitesourcesoftware.com/vulnerability-database/CVE-2019-0820

The dotnet commit that fixed the vulnerability is https://github.com/dotnet/corefx/commit/19d4b1163d8a03dd90ff5fd1785eea6305112545

### Issue:
We use whitesource and it has caught this issue with high severity. We don't consume System.Text.RegularExpressions directly but packages that use this. Therefore as a transitive dependency due to NetStandard library, which is being used by several other dotnet packages like Castle Windsor, MassTransit etc., Once an update is available the others could followup and update.

### Code:

[The latest version 2.0.3 of Net standard ](https://www.nuget.org/packages/NETStandard.Library/) still seem to be using System.Text.RegularExpressions version 4.3.0 as per https://github.com/dotnet/standard/blob/master/src/apicompat/netstandard/netstandard.depproj

### Fix
Please update[ library](https://www.nuget.org/packages/NETStandard.Library/) targeting .netStandard 1.6 to update System.Text.RegularExpression package to latest secured version 4.3.1 to fix the security issue or kindly suggest alternatives.

Issues.Title: linq using GetValueOrDefault  in Where clause problem
Issues.Body:
Hello,

I am currently using .NET core 2.2.x and EF Core. 2.2.6. I have a function that returns a List<Animal> from the database with no issue. It returns 11 results. However, when I try to use `.Where(p => p.DeletedAt.GetValueOrDefault(DateTime.Now) => DateTime.Now).ToList()`, it still should return 11 results, however it returns 0. I also eliminated the possibility that there is something wrong with my where clause (logic) because it works perfectly on 4.6.1 EF Core 2.2.6. Furthermore, I confirmed that it is only where I am comparing a nullable type using that function and I am guessing that I missed a thread someone opened on this issue. I am aware .NET core 2.2 is not LTS. I also thought this goes here because it's not AFAIK, an EF core issue but rather an Ienumerable/Linq issue.

Update: As it turns out your notion of `DateTime.Now` getting evaluated twice is true. To rectify that, I will now be using `DateTime.Now.Date`. This is odd because this exact code works on 4.6.1. You're probably right. SMH. Thank you @GrabYourPitchforks! You may now close.

Issues.Title: Strong name signature not valid
Issues.Body:
Since I've ported a ClickOnce application from .NET Framework 4.6.1 to .NET Standard 2.0, the message _"Strong assembly name signature not valid for **Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll**"_ appears when trying to install or update the application. So the next step was to verify the assembly strong name by using the [Strong Name Tool](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/framework/tools/sn-exe-strong-name-tool) to make sure, that everything is fine, but:

```sh

Microsoft (R) .NET Framework Strong Name Utility Version 4.0.30319.0
Copyright (c) Microsoft Corporation. All rights reserved.

Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll is a delay-signed or test-signed assembly
```

Additional information:

- The assembly versions `161.46041.41` and `161.46367.54` ended up in the same result
- This issue looks very similar to [this](https://www.damirscorner.com/blog/posts/20140502-StrongNameValidationFailedSecurityException.html)
- @markingmyname / @olprod: The root package, which is required for [Server Management Objects (SMOs)](https://docs.microsoft.com/sql/relational-databases/server-management-objects-smo/overview-smo?view=sql-server-ver15), is:

        - **Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll**

Issues.Title: System.Drawing.Printing.PrinterSettings slow
Issues.Body:
_This issue has been moved from [a ticket on Developer Community](https://developercommunity2.visualstudio.com/t/SystemDrawingPrintingPrinterSettings-/890524)._ --- Hello I'm debugging a problem with the printer settings. Some calls are significant slower if the default printer is a network printer, even if I explicit set a local printer name. After studying referencesource I think I found the culprit. I call: var printerSettings = new System.Drawing.Printing.PrinterSettings(); printerSettings.PrinterName = "LOCALPRINTER"; // the next call is slow if the OS default printer is a network printer var res = printerSettings.DefaultPageSettings.PrinterResolution Internally FastDeviceCapabilities is called. FastDeviceCapabilities calls GetOutputPort. But GetOutput port return the port of the default printer and not the port of the given printer! In addition, DeviceCapabilities is then called with a wrong combination of printer name and port, don't know if this could lead to additional problems. Resolution: GetOutputPort should return the port of the given printer and not accessing the default printer at all. Best Regards, Raphael --- ### Original Comments #### Raphael Affolter on 1/20/2020, 04:03 AM:

I forgot to mention: .Net Framework 4.6.1

Issues.Title: Build issues when referencing project that targets multiple frameworks C# WPF
Issues.Body:
I'm working on converting a large WPF solution's projects to SDK style and ran into some issues.

The solution is large with multiple projects(old style) all targeting .net452 and some nugets(some made by me) installed, targeting both .net452 and .netstandard2.1 This all seems to work fine, somehow the nuget manages to install the correct version targeting .net452.

I have decided to slowly convert the projects inside the solution to SDK style targeting .net452 and .netstandard2.1 just like the nugets.

This is where the problem starts, one project was converted so far that is referenced by multiple other projects. Localy everything seems to build and run fine, however when Azure DevOps(VS version 2019) is used to build the solution there are 2 scenarios:

1. The famous error message is shown:

                "Error CS0012: The type 'Object' is defined in an assembly that is not referenced. You must add a reference to assembly 
                 'netstandard, Version=2.1.0.0"

2. It builds fine but on app launch it crashes with:

                 "Could not load file or assembly 'netstandard, Version=2.1.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=cc7b13ffcd2ddd51' 
                 or one of its dependencies. The system cannot find the file specified."

I'm suspecting that the problem is related to referencing the SDK project, it looks like that somehow it references the .netstandard2.1 instead of the .net452.

The reason this is my suspicion is that if targetframework is set to only .net452 on the referenced project everything works fine. Google has led me to two possible solutions to tell the project what framework to use from the reference:

```
<ProjectReference Include="..\..\..\..\foo\foo.csproj"
                  AdditionalProperties="TargetFramework=net452">
      <Project>{xxxxxx-xxxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxxxx}</Project>
      <Name>foo</Name>
</ProjectReference>
```
and

```
<ProjectReference Include="..\..\..\..\foo\foo.csproj">
      <SetTargetFramework>TargetFramework=net452</SetTargetFramework>
      <Project>{xxxxxx-xxxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxxxx}</Project>
      <<Name>foo</Name>
</ProjectReference>
```
This doesn't look like it's doing anything and the problem still persists. At the moment I ran out of ideas and I'm here asking for help. Please let me know what I'm doing wrong or what else I can try.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Build issues when referencing project that targets multiple frameworks C# WPF" (#1776)

**TL;DR;** Requesting to add [FabricBot](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/fabricbot_overview) configuration associated with your repository to `.github/fabricbot.json`.

**Context**

FabricBot is now a [config-as-code-only](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/bot-config-as-code) platform. As a result, while you can still use the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/corefx) to modify your FabricBot configuration, you can no longer save the changes. The only way to save changes to your configuration at the moment is to _export configuration_ from the portal and upload the exported configuration to `.github/fabricbot.json` in your repository. In this pull request, we are adding your FabricBot configuration to your repository at `.github/fabricbot.json` so that you can make changes to it going forward.

While the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/corefx) is the *only way* to modify your FabricBot configuration at the moment, we have a feature on our backlog to publish the JSON schema defining the structure of the FabricBot configuration file. With the JSON schema, you can (1) use a plaintext editor of your choice to modify the FabricBot configuration file and use the schema to validate the file after editing or (2) [configure](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/languages/json#_json-schemas-and-settings) VS Code to use the schema when editing FabricBot configuration file to take advantage of convenience features such as automatic code completion and field description on mouseover.

Issues.Title: Fix RSA OAEP decryption in OpenSSL with non-power-of-two keys lengths
Issues.Body:
## Customer Impact

A customer reported in dotnet/runtime#71607 that decrypting RSA OAEP with SHA2 and a 3072-bit key on Linux resulted in a OAEP de-padding error, while other platforms were able to perform these operations successfully.

Investigation in to the issue led to uncover that RSA OAEP decryption that uses the managed implementation does not work with non-power-of-two keys because we do not slice a rented buffer accordingly. The current implementation only works because `CryptoPool.Rent` happens to give back power-of-two arrays which are exactly the same size as the key.

The fix is to slice the data to the correct size.

This does not affect dotnet/runtime because the managed implementation of RSA OAEP is no longer used for OpenSSL RSA decryption. This change was introduced in dotnet/runtime#50063.

## Testing

Unit tests were introduced to test RSA OAEP encryption with a 3072-bit RSA key. These tests will be forward-ported to dotnet/runtime.

## Risk

Minimal. The change is localized and understood that a `Slice` was missing.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "Fix RSA OAEP decryption in OpenSSL with non-power-of-two keys lengths" (#43153)

Issues.Title: Reduce JIT during LSP initialize with generated JSON metadata
Issues.Body:
The LSP initialize handshake serializes the client and server capability graphs through System.Text.Json reflection. In Visual Studio this emits several hundred dynamic property accessors and constructors that are jitted on first use, which shows up in the RebuildSolution RPS JIT count.

Adds a source generated context for the startup types and puts it ahead of the existing resolver in `AddLspSerializerOptions`. Types outside the context still fall back to reflection, so extension payloads keep working.

Issues.Title: Do not report IDE0060 for parameters referenced in [InterpolatedStringHandlerArgument]
Issues.Body:

### Description
When a method has a parameter referenced by [InterpolatedStringHandlerArgument(paramName)] on an interpolated string handler parameter in the same method signature, the parameter is passed to the handler at call sites. Removing the parameter breaks caller call-sites and method signatures.

Issues.Title: Fix NRE in VisualBasicRemoveUnnecessaryCastDiagnosticAnalyzer (Fixes #77134)
Issues.Body:
Fixes #77134

### Summary
When analyzing a Visual Basic document where _semanticModel.Compilation, castType, or parameterType.ElementType is null (such as in embedded resource files or detached/speculative semantic models), CastPassedToParamArrayDefinitelyCantBeRemoved threw a NullReferenceException.

In Visual Basic .NET, invoking an extension method via receiver syntax _semanticModel.Compilation.ClassifyConversion(...) emits a runtime receiver null check at the call-site, causing an unhandled NullReferenceException in the analyzer.

### Changes
- In CastAnalyzer.vb (CastPassedToParamArrayDefinitelyCantBeRemoved), safely guarded _semanticModel.Compilation, castType, and parameterType.ElementType against null before calling ClassifyConversion.
- Added unit test TestRemoveUnnecessaryCast_QueryHelper to RemoveUnnecessaryCastTests.vb verifying the scenario reported in #77134.

### Verification
- Tested with Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.VisualBasic.CodeStyle.UnitTests:
  - TestRemoveUnnecessaryCast_QueryHelper: Passed.
  - Full RemoveUnnecessaryCast suite: 127 Passed, 3 Skipped, 0 Failed.

Issues.Title: Preserve owned test processes and collect timeout dumps after launcher exit
Issues.Body:
**Timeout dump proof succeeded. Temporary probes are removed, and the final-code process controls pass in ordinary Windows and Linux CI. The PR remains draft because ordinary CI also has unrelated Windows test failures.**

Build [1641311](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1641311) includes the latest Tool Help discovery changes, but its single-machine Windows job reached the global deadline, reported an exited launcher, and stalled until Azure canceled it. Dump copying found zero files and the published log artifact was empty. A controlled reproduction using that exact unfixed RunTests revision reproduces exited-launcher discovery failure, zero dumps, a surviving managed child, and blocked completion.

Establish ownership before test startup using Windows jobs / Unix process groups, retain verified descendant identities after launcher exit, separate process exit from redirected-output draining, bound collectors and cleanup, and persist stage-specific diagnostics throughout execution. Ownership is established before target startup hooks run; target environment values travel over stdin rather than appearing in command lines. Production test deadlines and the user-cancellation distinction are preserved.

Actual CI evidence for product candidate `44de8bc3efa`:

| Proof | Run | Downloaded debugger evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Hung host, hung child, exited launcher on Windows CoreCLR, Windows .NET Framework, and Linux CoreCLR | [1642963](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1642963) | All fifteen intended target dumps contain the expected managed hang frames. |
| Actual 90-minute global deadline with launcher already exited | [1642963](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1642963) | Host PID 1304: 171,042,418 bytes; child PID 2560: 87,214,260 bytes. Both opened at HungTestHost/HungChild; all six target dumps completed approximately seven seconds after the deadline, followed by cleanup and publication before Azure's 120-minute limit. |
| Actual 25-minute VSTest inactivity deadline | [1643025](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1643025) | Host PID 4648: 157,070,594 bytes, opened at HungTestHost; cleanup and publication completed. This reran a corrected temporary log-marker assertion without changing product code. |

Artifacts:
https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1642963&view=artifacts
https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1643025&view=artifacts

Temporary pipeline/timeout probes and probe-specific environment injection are removed in `e919ca590a1`. Permanent process controls remain, including deterministic coverage of identity mismatch, output-completion races, and PID-file publication sharing.

Final ordinary CI [1643056](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1643056) completed: both Linux single-machine jobs succeeded, and all sixteen permanent controls passed in Windows CoreCLR Helix. The overall run failed in the Windows debug Helix monitor on unchanged `IncrementalParsingTests.TestChangeDefineAndIfElse` and `OperatorCompletionProviderTests.OperatorInfixOfferingsAndCompletions` tests. No unrelated fixes are included.

Issues.Title: File-based apps: dotnet run reuses cached build when a required dependency DLL is missing
Issues.Body:
### Describe the bug

`dotnet run --file` reuses the cached build of a file-based app even when a required package dependency DLL is missing from the cached output directory. It then crashes with `FileNotFoundException`, instead of rebuilding/copying the missing dependency.

This was first observed with a small file-based utility referencing `NuGet.Configuration` and `NuGet.Packaging`. The cause of the original DLL disappearance is unknown. The following minimal repro deliberately removes one output DLL to demonstrate the cache-validation problem deterministically; it does not delete anything from the global NuGet package cache.

### Steps to reproduce

On Windows with PowerShell, create `repro.cs` in an otherwise empty directory:

```csharp
#:package NuGet.Configuration@7.3.1

Console.WriteLine(typeof(NuGet.Configuration.Settings).Assembly.Location);
```

Run:

```powershell
# Build and run successfully; capture the copied dependency's location.
$dll = dotnet run --file .\repro.cs | Select-Object -Last 1
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0 -or !(Test-Path -LiteralPath $dll)) {
    throw "Initial run failed or dependency path was not found."
}

# Remove only this file-based app's copied dependency DLL.
# The path printed above is under:
# %TEMP%\dotnet\runfile\repro-<hash>\bin\debug\NuGet.Configuration.dll
Remove-Item -LiteralPath $dll

# No source/input changes. This reuses the incomplete cache and crashes.
dotnet run --file .\repro.cs

# Force the build: succeeds and restores the missing DLL.
dotnet run --no-cache --file .\repro.cs
Test-Path -LiteralPath $dll # True
```

The `Assembly.Location` access may produce an IL3000 warning on the initial build; the normal `dotnet run` execution nevertheless prints the DLL's actual path. This exact minimal program was tested successfully before deleting the DLL, failed after deleting it, and succeeded again with `--no-cache`.

### Expected behavior

Without `--no-build`, `dotnet run --file` detects that a required runtime output is missing, invokes the build to restore it, and runs successfully. An incomplete cached build should not be considered up to date.

### Actual behavior

The second normal run skips the build and fails:

```text
Unhandled exception. System.IO.FileNotFoundException: Could not load file or assembly 'NuGet.Configuration, Version=7.3.1.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=31bf3856ad364e35'. The system cannot find the file specified.
File name: 'NuGet.Configuration, Version=7.3.1.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=31bf3856ad364e35'
Requested by: sdk-missing-dependency-repro, Version=1.0.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=null
 --> System.Private.CoreLib, Version=11.0.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=7cec85d7bea7798e
   at Program.<Main>$(String[] args)
```

The host also reports that it cannot open `%TEMP%\dotnet\runfile\<app>-<hash>\bin\debug\NuGet.Configuration.dll` with error `0x80070002`.

Exit code observed: `-532462766`.

### Is this a regression?

Unknown; verified with SDK `11.0.100-rc.2.26504.105`. Other SDK versions have not been tested.

### Are there any workarounds?

Use `dotnet run --no-cache --file .\repro.cs`. This restores the missing DLL and runs successfully, but forces the build on every invocation.

### Environment

```text
.NET SDK:
 Version:         11.0.100-rc.2.26504.105
 Commit:          820230c386
 MSBuild version: 18.12.0-1.26504.105+820230c38

Runtime Environment:
 OS Name:         Windows
 OS Version:      10.0.26300
 OS Platform:     Windows
 RID:             win-x64

Host:
 Version:         11.0.0-rc.2.26504.105
 Architecture:    x64
 Commit:          820230c386

Environment variables:
 DOTNET_ROLL_FORWARD_TO_PRERELEASE=1

global.json:
 Not found
```

Reproduced from the command line without an IDE.

### Related issue

Possibly related symptoms: dotnet/sdk#53732. That issue was closed after a fix involving `#:project` dependency changes. This repro uses only a direct `#:package` reference, no referenced projects, no concurrent execution, and an explicitly removed runtime output on a newer SDK.

Issues.Title: Add adaptive CI failure attribution skill
Issues.Body:
## Problem

A failing CI run can be caused by a recent change, an older issue, an occasional failure, or a problem with the build service. One retry or an older similar failure alone doesn't show which explanation is right.

## Description

Add a read-only skill that guides agents through CI failures. It helps them confirm which code and build were tested, look into each failure, and gather only the evidence needed to distinguish possible causes.

The skill also explains how to compare runs, describe confidence and evidence gaps, and avoid claiming that a change had no effect unless the evidence supports that conclusion.

| MSTest | `4.5.0-preview.26503.3` | `4.6.0-preview.26519.1` |
| MSTest.Sdk | `4.5.0-preview.26503.3` | `4.6.0-preview.26519.1` |

All three new packages identify TestFx revision [`d25ab5d76da4d7202291e5d1af1070b5496751a9`](https://github.com/microsoft/testfx/commit/d25ab5d76da4d7202291e5d1af1070b5496751a9), which contains [`8718afe9`](https://github.com/microsoft/testfx/commit/8718afe9b99b11e5b36be7dbc8d9e9ca959b3982) from microsoft/testfx#11932. The published package metadata was checked in the repository's existing `test-tools` feed, not inferred from version/date alone. The inspected `2.5.2` servicing previews do not contain this fix.

The upstream reader treats socket reset/abort during transport reads as EOF, clears partial frames, and lets the server loop complete. Unrelated IO failures, invalid frames, and deserializer errors remain errors. This closes the reset-before-lifetime-cancellation window described in the linked investigation without masking process exit 134 or disabling crash dumps.

Keep MTP, MSTest, and MSTest.Sdk on the same producer revision per the existing NativeAOT/source-generator coherency requirement. Update the authoritative dependency manifest and `global.json`; regenerate `eng/Version.Details.props` using Darc's `DependencyFileManager.GenerateVersionDetailsProps` API. No feed changes or SDK-side transport workarounds.

## Validation

Revision: `f6951c73f5f33e14c4174c4cc5636859cd9b294a`, Windows x64, pinned SDK `12.0.100-alpha.1.26480.102`, Debug redist.

| Exact command | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `.\build.cmd /bl:artifacts\log\mtp-sdk-build.binlog` | Passed; full SDK/redist build, 0 errors. |
| `.\.dotnet\dotnet.exe build test\dotnet.Tests\dotnet.Tests.csproj -c Debug -bl:artifacts\log\mtp-dotnet-tests-build.binlog --verbosity minimal` | Passed; 0 errors. |
| `.\.dotnet\dotnet.exe scripts\RunTests.cs -- --project test\dotnet.Tests\dotnet.Tests.csproj --filter 'FullyQualifiedName~TestApplicationHandlerTests\|FullyQualifiedName~TestApplicationLaunchTests'` | 95 executed, 95 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped. |
| `.\.dotnet\dotnet.exe scripts\RunTests.cs -- --project test\dotnet.Tests\dotnet.Tests.csproj --filter 'FullyQualifiedName~RunTestProjectWithTests_ShouldReturnExitCodeSuccess\|FullyQualifiedName~RunTestProjectWithWithRetryFeature_ShouldSucceed'` | 4 executed, 4 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped: ordinary and retry-enabled test runs, each in Debug and Release. All four child `dotnet test` commands exited 0. |
| `git diff --cached --check` | Passed before commit. |

The test project's assets resolve MTP `2.6.0-preview.26519.1` and MSTest framework/adapter `4.6.0-preview.26519.1` from its effective package cache. The MTP DLL beside `dotnet.Tests.dll` is byte-identical to the package's `lib/net11.0` DLL selected for the net12.0 test host.

The build reports existing dependency-audit warnings; no audit settings or unrelated dependencies were changed. Linux Helix reproduction and NativeAOT-specific execution were **not** performed locally; CI remains necessary.

## Test-value evidence

An isolated, unchanged transport probe invoked the shipped `NamedPipeConnectionBase.ReadNextMessageAsync` through reflection, using streams that raise the exact `IOException`/inner `SocketException` reset or abort before cancellation. This is injected-transport evidence, **not** a claim of reproducing the Linux kernel timing race.

The same 13 cases ran against both published package binaries (and again against the new DLL in the SDK test-host layout), with the same assertions:

| Cases | Old package | New package |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PeerDisconnect_{ConnectionReset,ConnectionAborted}_Prefix{0,2,6}`: require EOF and successful decoding of a subsequent complete frame | 6 failures: `IOException: Peer disconnected.` | 6 passed |
| `UnrelatedIoFailure_Socket{False,True}_Prefix{0,6}`: require the original unrelated IO exception | 4 passed | 4 passed |
| `InvalidFrameLength_{-1,0,3}`: require the exact invalid-frame exception | 3 passed | 3 passed |
| Total / process exit | 13 executed, 7 passed, 6 failed, 0 skipped; exit 1 | 13 executed, 13 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped; exit 0 |

Producer revisions were read from each loaded assembly's informational version: old `7e5205486fd185a1f205c311183a55a6b3eb99df`, new `d25ab5d76da4d7202291e5d1af1070b5496751a9`. The comparison ran both net8.0 package assets on .NET 8, then old net9.0 versus the new net11.0 test-host DLL on the repo's .NET 12 runtime, with the same results. Existing source regression tests live in TestFx's `NamedPipeConnectionTests`; this SDK change only consumes the fixed packages.

Independent follow-up to dotnet/sdk#56725; it does not modify that PR's static-web-assets fix.

Issues.Title: Backport distinct Copilot CLI and VS Code agent detection to .NET 10
Issues.Body:
## Problem

The .NET 10 `release/10.0.4xx` detector recognizes `COPILOT_CLI=1` but emits the legacy `copilot` label. It does not recognize the VS Code agent signals `COPILOT_AGENT` or `AI_AGENT=github_copilot_vscode_agent`.

Newer SDK code distinguishes `copilot-cli` from `copilot-vscode`. Backporting this distinction would improve detection coverage and make agent attribution consistent across SDK generations.

## Proposed change

Backport the Copilot-specific detection and label changes from #54358 and #54659 to the appropriate supported .NET 10 SDK servicing branches, without bringing in unrelated agent-detection changes. Emit `copilot-cli` for CLI signals and `copilot-vscode` for VS Code signals. Preserve the existing `copilot-app` detection backported in #55443 and the ability to report multiple matching agents.

Include coverage for CLI-only, VS Code-only, App, overlapping signals, and no-agent environments.

## Behavior considerations

This is not exclusively a telemetry change: detecting an agent also affects MSBuild live node display and Microsoft.Testing.Platform ANSI output. Validate and document those effects for newly recognized environments.

The backport only improves future reporting from updated SDKs. Consumers must continue handling the legacy `copilot` label; historical data cannot universally distinguish the clients because some earlier implementations used that label for both.

Related: #53032, #54348, #54276.

The test runner's `build.binlog` captures the test project build, not necessarily builds performed by tests. When those scenario builds fail, their logs may not be available for diagnosis unless tests are changed to request binlogs.

Add opt-in `--test-binlogs` support to capture build logs from `MSBuildCommand` and `DotnetBuildCommand`. Issues.Title: Add SDK-generated fallback for the Hot Reload settings endpoint
Issues.Body:
Possible fix for https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/69718.

## Problem

After https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/pull/56118, .NET 11 SDK generates Blazor browser-tools initializers when Hot Reload build outputs are enabled (by default in Debug builds). This also happens for ordinary `dotnet run` launches and projects targeting older frameworks, since SDK selection is independent of the target framework.

When an initializer probes `/_framework/dotnet-browser-tools/hot-reload-settings.json`, older hosts lack the disabled-settings endpoint supplied by .NET 11 ASP.NET Core hosts. The initializer correctly treats the failed request as Hot Reload being disabled, but the browser still reports a 404.

## Change

For pre-.NET 11 targets, generate a constant `{"hotReload": false}` static asset at the existing settings URL. Generation uses the existing browser-tools gate, including `EnableHotReloadInRuntimeConfigDevFile`. The asset is build-only, excluded from publish output, and reused without rewriting on incremental builds.

Net11+ targets continue using their existing host fallback. Their non-Development behavior is unchanged.

## Behavior preservation

- **Active watch providers retain precedence.** ASP.NET Core and legacy DevServer forwarding runs before static assets. Gateway’s provider proxy uses order `-1000`, ahead of static asset endpoints at `-100`.
- **No activation state is written into build output.** The generated file always contains `false`. The provider supplies `true` dynamically, preserving the same build output across ordinary and watch launches.
- **Default Release and publish behavior remain unchanged.** The fallback follows the existing Hot Reload generation gate and never reaches published applications.

## Validation

All Web/WASM regression cases covering net8 and net10 fail without the fix and pass with it. All 32 focused integration tests and 12 real-browser run/watch scenarios pass, including state-preserving live edits.

Issues.Title: Drain watch test process output through stream EOF
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Fix the process-output race behind `MobileHotReloadTests.CtrlC_ShutsDownCleanly` in dotnet/sdk#56715.

`AwaitableProcess` cancelled output reads when the process exited, although stdout/stderr callbacks could still be delivering the final lines. The test could therefore miss the exit trace even when watch shut down successfully.

- Complete the channel only after both redirected streams reach EOF.
- Drain buffered output before reporting that the required line is missing.
- Preserve timeout and disposal cancellation, and do not emit synthetic empty lines for EOF notifications.
- Document process-output completion semantics.

## Validation

- **3 deterministic regression tests passed on Windows x64 across three runs, none skipped.**
- Tests hold stdout/stderr delivery behind a gate until the child has definitely exited, rather than depending on timing or sleeps.
- All three tests fail with the original helper and pass with this fix.
- Whitespace and documentation-link validation passed.

Independent follow-up to dotnet/sdk#56715. The full watch integration suite and non-Windows execution have not been rerun locally.

Issues.Title: Warn about forward slashes in template symbol and choice names
Issues.Body:
Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/templating/issues/3127

Template localization uses `/` to separate key segments, so symbol names and choice values containing `/` cannot be addressed correctly. Template validation currently gives authors no warning about these names.

Add mandatory validation warnings for symbol names (`MV013`) and choice values (`MV014`) containing a forward slash. The diagnostics identify the offending names and explain the localization restriction. They run during scanning and instantiation and leave templates valid for compatibility. Document the restriction in the template configuration reference and localization guide, and generate the XLF updates from the new English resources.

Validation:
- Before the fix, five of the initial seven regression cases failed because no warning was emitted.
- The final `RunnableProjectConfigTests` class passed all 19 tests on both `net12.0` and `net481`, with no skips and no build warnings or errors. The 12 new cases cover ordinary names, other separators, leading/trailing slashes, choices, computed symbols, and both validation scopes.
- Tests ran through `scripts/RunTests.cs` with `--skip-redist-check`; these cases load template configurations against a virtual file system and do not execute the assembled SDK. Full SDK integration tests were not run.
- `UpdateXlf` and `git diff --check` passed.

Issues.Title: Preserve template verifier command error codes
Issues.Body:
Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/templating/issues/8593

Template Verifier currently reports `InstantiationFailed` for both installation and instantiation failures, even when `dotnet new` returns a more specific error such as `TemplateDoesNotExist` or `InvalidOption`.

Preserve exit codes defined in `TemplateVerificationErrorCode`. For unrecognized exit codes, fall back to `InstallFailed` during installation and `InstantiationFailed` during instantiation. The existing instantiation failure test now uses its configured command runner, and regression cases cover known codes, unknown codes, and stopping after installation fails.

Validation:
- The eight focused failure cases changed from five failures before the fix to eight passes after it; the test project built with no warnings or errors.
- The full unit project had ten passes and two failures. Both failures occurred during existing `TestBase` initialization because the locally built SDK layout (`artifacts/bin/redist/Debug/dotnet/dotnet.exe`) was unavailable, before the verifier ran.

Issues.Title: tasks: sign OpenHarmony ELF build outputs
Issues.Body:
### Summary

OpenHarmony devices only execute signed ELF binaries, and a changed signed
binary fails with EPERM, so build and publish outputs must be re-signed in
place. Add an `OpenHarmonyCodesign` MSBuild task and a targets hook that
signs the output tree for `openharmony-*` RIDs, mirroring the macOS codesign
hook. Non-ELF files, symbolic links and still-valid `.codesign` sections are
skipped; the SingleFile trailer is preserved.

### Changes

- `src/Tasks/Microsoft.NET.Build.Tasks/OpenHarmonyCodesign.cs`: the task that
  walks the target/publish directories and signs the ELF outputs.
- `src/Tasks/Microsoft.NET.Build.Tasks/ElfSigner.cs`: ELF64 parsing and the
  `.codesign` section writer (headers guarded, size checks, signature
  validation).
- `src/Tasks/Microsoft.NET.Build.Tasks/targets/Microsoft.NET.Sdk.targets`:
  `_OpenHarmonyCodeSignBuildOutputs` and `_OpenHarmonyCodeSignPublishOutputs`,
  with the stamps registered in `FileWrites` (mirrors `_EnableMacOSCodeSign`).
- `src/Tasks/Common/Resources/Strings.resx` and the 13 `.xlf` files:
  NETSDK1247-NETSDK1250 for the signer diagnostics.
- Seventeen files, 1738 insertions and 1 deletion.

### Impact

- Only when the runtime identifier (or apphost RID) starts with `openharmony`;
  other platforms and non-ELF outputs are unchanged.
- Non-ELF files, symbolic links, foreign signatures and already-valid
  signatures are left untouched.

### Test

```
$ dotnet publish -r openharmony-arm64
$ <ELF section reader> bin/Release/net11.0/openharmony-arm64/publish/hello
bin/Release/net11.0/openharmony-arm64/publish/hello: VALID (flags=0x10, root=..., sig=...)
```

- The published apphost carries a valid `.codesign` section; the managed
  assemblies are not ELF and are left untouched.

### Scope note

This is S1c from the OpenHarmony port plan (dotnet/runtime#132866). The signer
is currently kept downstream by default; opening it here for the maintainers'
call — if it should stay downstream, close this PR.

> [!NOTE]
> This PR was authored with AI assistance (agent tooling) under the author's direction.

Issues.Title: OpenHarmony: SDK sandbox defaults and build without installers/workloads
Issues.Body:
### Summary

Bake the OpenHarmony sandbox defaults into the SDK (JIT W^X off, invariant
globalization, telemetry/nologo opt-outs), and build the SDK for openharmony
without installers, workloads or NativeAOT.

### Changes

- `OpenHarmonyEnvironmentDefaults` applies the defaults to the CLI process and
  every child process it spawns; the redist runtimeconfig carries
  `System.Runtime.EnableWriteXorExecute=false` and
  `System.Globalization.Invariant=true`, which
  `GenerateCliRuntimeConfigurationFiles` copies into the bundled tools. TMPDIR
  is deliberately not set: the runtime reads the host-provided value through
  `Path.GetTempPath()`.
- Build: skip the installers for openharmony RIDs; use the product-moniker RID
  for the shared framework and the openharmony RID list lookups; skip the
  bundled/builtin workload manifest packs and the layout's no-manifest error;
  map the openharmony TargetOS to `linux` for the layout crossgen2; set
  `NativeAotSupported=false` for openharmony centrally; `dn` publishes AOT only
  where the toolchain exists; the pack-version aliases can be overridden from
  the command line for a locally built runtime.
- Tests: `OpenHarmonyEnvironmentDefaultsTests`.
- Own delta: 17 files, 182 insertions and 15 deletions (stacked on the RID
  graph PR).

### Impact

- OpenHarmony only; other SDK builds are unchanged.
- The SDK runs on OHOS without external environment variables, and its build
  does not require installers, workloads or a NativeAOT toolchain.

### Test

1. Run the SDK on OHOS: the CLI works without external environment variables,
   and the bundled tools' runtimeconfig contains the two defaults.
2. Build the SDK for `openharmony-arm64`: no installers/workloads/NativeAOT are
   produced and the layout completes.
3. `OpenHarmonyEnvironmentDefaultsTests` pass.

> [!NOTE]
> This PR was authored with AI assistance (agent tooling) under the author's direction.

Stacked on #56732: until that PR merges, this diff also includes its RID-graph commit.

Issues.Body:
## Summary

Fix the endpoint-input mutation behind the macOS SWA diagnostic logger failure observed in dotnet/sdk#56715.

`ComputeEndpointsForReferenceStaticWebAssets` aliased `CandidateEndpoints`, replaced entries, and assigned null to endpoints whose assets were not found. MSBuild can retain that input array for asynchronous logging, producing `MSB4017` / `NullReferenceException` while formatting task parameters.

- Collect retained endpoints into a separate output list.
- Return no null entries and preserve candidate arrays, routes, and metadata.
- Keep endpoint ordering and existing base-path behavior.
- Document task input/output ownership.

## Validation

- **9 focused task tests passed on Windows x64, none skipped.**
- The original source fails four strengthened/new filtering and input-immutability cases; the fixed source passes all nine.
- The `net472` task build passed with no warnings.
- Documentation links and whitespace checks passed.

Independent follow-up to dotnet/sdk#56715. The original macOS diagnostic build has not been rerun locally.

Issues.Title: [release/10.0.1xx] Check each referenced project once in dotnet format
Issues.Body:
Backport of #56621 to `release/10.0.1xx`. Fixes #56363 for .NET 10.

Draft until #56621 merges to `main`.

## Description

Before running analyzers, `dotnet format style` / `dotnet format analyzers` checks that every referenced project loaded by recursively walking `ProjectReferences`. The walk never remembers which projects it already checked, so a shared dependency is re-walked once per path that reaches it, which is exponential in the depth of the reference graph.

This replaces the recursion with a single pass over the project and its transitive dependencies from the solution's cached `ProjectDependencyGraph`, so each project is checked once.

This is a manual port, not a cherry-pick. On this branch the check is the synchronous `AllReferencedProjectsLoaded` (an `mscorlib.dll` metadata-reference check) under `src/BuiltInTools/dotnet-format`, rather than the async compilation check on `main`. The port keeps this branch's check exactly as is and changes only how the graph is walked. The test is translated from MSTest to xUnit.

## Customer Impact

On solutions with dense project-reference graphs (for example, ones using `DisableTransitiveProjectReferences`), `dotnet format style` / `analyzers` runs for minutes to hours. #56363 reports 11.5 minutes on a 30-project repro and 14+ hours on a 380-project solution. Teams that use `dotnet format --verify-no-changes` as a CI gate can't run it. The only workarounds are formatting project by project or skipping the analyzer passes.

## Regression?

No. The unmemoized walk is long-standing; it is also present in .NET 8 (`dotnet/format`).

## Risk

Low. The change is limited to the pre-analysis reference check. The set of projects checked is the same (the project plus its transitive project references), and so is the per-project check. Any dependency that fails the check still skips the project with the existing "required references did not load" warning.

## Testing

New `AnalyzerRunnerTests`: a dense 40-project graph (each project references every earlier one) completes in seconds; without the fix it effectively never finishes and the test harness's hang detection trips.

Issues.Title: Fix endpoint tests under compression-like temporary paths
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Fix the intermittent `Build_DefaultDocumentAndSpaFallback_CreatesAdditionalEndpoints` failure reported in dotnet/sdk#54914 and seen again in dotnet/sdk#56715.

The test filtered full asset paths with `Contains(".br")` and `Contains(".gz")`. A random parent directory such as `xgupjmah.bre` therefore excluded valid uncompressed `index.html` endpoints, even though the CI binlog showed they were generated correctly.

- Match the asset filename instead of substrings in the full path.
- Run the integration test under explicit `.br` and `.gz` parent paths.
- Preserve the original route, SPA fallback order, and full manifest baseline assertions.
- Add contributor guidance about extension checks in temporary paths.

## Validation

- Both regression cases fail with the original predicate and pass with this fix.
- **2 integration tests passed on Windows x64, none skipped**, using current repo SDK targets and the unchanged manifest baseline.
- Whitespace validation passed.

Independent follow-up to dotnet/sdk#56715; no dependency on its localization changes.

Issues.Title: [dotnet watch] Reload the project graph for the selected device and runtime identifier
Issues.Body:
Depends on #56722. Addresses the RID-specific output lookup described in [this review comment](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/pull/56722#discussion_r4328313870).

An iOS project can default to a simulator RID, such as `iossimulator-arm64`. When a user runs `dotnet watch` and selects a physical iPhone instead of a simulator, restore and build use the device RID, `ios-arm64`. However, watch retains the project graph loaded before that selection, so it still reads the simulator's output paths. In #56722, this can make mobile WebSocket authentication read missing or stale keys rather than the key pair included in the device build.

Reload the graph after device selection and restore, using the selected `Device` and `RuntimeIdentifier`. Keep those values for later graph loads and rebuilds.

Add regression coverage for matching and changed RIDs, device-ID escaping, and preselected devices. The RID tests do not require a mobile SDK or physical device.

### Validation

- Reproduced the original failure before the fix: the matching-RID control passed; the changed-RID case failed on the intermediate output path assertion.
- Built the SDK and ran focused build, framework/device selection, graph, and restart tests with this fix above #56722: 49 passed, 0 failed, 2 existing skips.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "[dotnet watch] Reload the project graph for the selected device and runtime identifier" (#56723)

Issues.Title: [dotnet watch] Align mobile WebSocket authentication with WASM browser tools
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Align mobile `dotnet watch` WebSocket authentication with the
build-owned key model introduced for WASM/browser tools in
https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/pull/56118.

- Generate and reuse an RSA key pair in the project's intermediate output.
- Supply the public key through the workload's existing
  `RuntimeEnvironmentVariable` items, rather than from watch.
- Verify the provider's secret echo before sending initialization or
  accepting Hot Reload updates.
- Share key creation and validation code between separate mobile and
  Static Web Assets tasks.

Browser refresh server behavior and `dotnet run -e` semantics remain
unchanged.

## Validation

- Built the SDK, including both injected-agent target frameworks.
- Ran focused key-generation, WebSocket, mobile watch, and browser
  regression tests.
- Reviewed current dotnet/android and dotnet/macios integration.
  Real-device execution was not performed.

Issues.Title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-96960 | .NET and Visual Studio Denial of Service Vulnerability
Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in System.Security.Cryptography.Xml; System.Private.Xml. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. Signed XML fixes add input-depth and operation-count limits, prohibit DTD processing by default, validate entity references, bound encrypted-data candidate processing, and cap attributes and namespaces used by C14N transforms. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/135711 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 7.5 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-405 (Asymmetric Resource Consumption (Amplification)) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Windows, Linux, macOS - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages The vulnerability affects Microsoft .NET projects that use an affected package version listed below. Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | --------------- [System.Security.Cryptography.Xml](https://www.nuget.org/packages/System.Security.Cryptography.Xml) | >= 10.0.0, <= 10.0.12 | 10.0.13 [System.Security.Cryptography.Xml](https://www.nuget.org/packages/System.Security.Cryptography.Xml) | >= 11.0.0-preview.1, <= 11.0.0-rc.1 | 11.0.0-rc.2 [System.Security.Cryptography.Xml](https://www.nuget.org/packages/System.Security.Cryptography.Xml) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.4 | 8.0.5 [System.Security.Cryptography.Xml](https://www.nuget.org/packages/System.Security.Cryptography.Xml) | >= 9.0.0, <= 9.0.20 | 9.0.21 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? If using a package listed in [affected packages](#affected-packages), you're exposed to the vulnerability. ### How do I fix the issue? 1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET. If you have installed one or more .NET SDKs through Visual Studio, Visual Studio will prompt you to update Visual Studio, which will also update your .NET SDKs. 2. If your application references the vulnerable package, update the package reference to the patched version. You can list the versions you have installed by running the `dotnet --info` command. * If you're using .NET 8.0, you should download and install .NET 8.0.32 Runtime or .NET 8.0.426 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/8.0. * If you're using .NET 9.0, you should download and install .NET 9.0.21 Runtime or .NET 9.0.319 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/9.0. * If you're using .NET 10.0, you should download and install .NET 10.0.13 Runtime or .NET 10.0.402 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/10.0. * If you're using .NET 11.0, you should download and install .NET 11.0.0-rc.2 Runtime or .NET 11.0.100-rc.2 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/11.0. Once you have installed the updated runtime or SDK, restart your apps for the update to take effect. Additionally, if you've deployed [self-contained applications](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/deploying/#self-contained-deployments-scd) targeting any of the impacted versions, these applications are also vulnerable and must be recompiled and redeployed. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. The main repos are located at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. Microsoft disclaims all warranties, either express or implied, including the warranties of merchantability and fitness for a particular purpose. In no event shall Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers be liable for any damages whatsoever including direct, indirect, incidental, consequential, loss of business profits or special damages, even if Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers have been advised of the possibility of such damages. Some states do not allow the exclusion or limitation of liability for consequential or incidental damages so the foregoing limitation may not apply. ### External Links [CVE-2026-96960](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-96960) ### Acknowledgements - Coşkun Bağrıaçık - Dr.-Ing Ashar Javed (@soaj1664ashar) ### Revisions V1.0 (10/13/2026): Advisory published.

If using a package listed in [affected packages](#affected-packages), you're exposed to the vulnerability. ### How do I fix the issue? 1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET. If you have installed one or more .NET SDKs through Visual Studio, Visual Studio will prompt you to update Visual Studio, which will also update your .NET SDKs. 2. If your application references the vulnerable package, update the package reference to the patched version. You can list the versions you have installed by running the `dotnet --info` command. * If you're using .NET 8.0, you should download and install .NET 8.0.32 Runtime or .NET 8.0.426 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/8.0. * If you're using .NET 9.0, you should download and install .NET 9.0.21 Runtime or .NET 9.0.319 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/9.0. * If you're using .NET 10.0, you should download and install .NET 10.0.13 Runtime or .NET 10.0.402 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/10.0. * If you're using .NET 11.0, you should download and install .NET 11.0.0-rc.2 Runtime or .NET 11.0.100-rc.2 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/11.0. Once you have installed the updated runtime or SDK, restart your apps for the update to take effect. Additionally, if you've deployed [self-contained applications](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/deploying/#self-contained-deployments-scd) targeting any of the impacted versions, these applications are also vulnerable and must be recompiled and redeployed. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization.
